title: Ukraine learns to fight without Starlink as Musk plays politics with satellites
gist: Starting October 13, 2026, SpaceX throttled military-grade Starlink in Ukraine for terminals moving faster than about 99 mph, reportedly on Musk's order. This disrupted drone strikes, resupply and interceptor air defense. Ukrainian and Western drone makers (BlueBird Tech, Buntar Aerospace, Quantum Systems) had already been building in redundancy through fiber-optic links, mesh radio, LTE/5G, optical comms and AI/GPS-free navigation. Europe is speeding up sovereign alternatives (OneWeb, IRIS², Project Bromo, SATCOMBw 4, ICEYE-Nokia), though none come close to Starlink's 10,000-satellite scale.

insights.claim: Starlink has let Ukraine maintain civilian and military communications and has expanded its ability to remotely control and guide drones for air defense and strikes on Russian targets. It is also deployed on Ukrainian ground robots and drone boats in the Black Sea.

themes.theme: October 2026 Starlink throttling and its battlefield impact

insights.claim: Since October 13, 2026, SpaceX has throttled military-grade Starlink service in Ukraine for terminals moving faster than about 99 mph (160 km/h). This was reportedly ordered by Elon Musk and possibly discussed with President Trump, while both Musk and the Trump administration deny responsibility and blame each other.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Starlink's availability is now a political variable, which damages SpaceX's reliability as a defense supplier in allies' eyes.

insights.claim: The Starlink throttling began without warning in the middle of the night and disrupted Ukrainian drone missions that supply frontline units, reconnaissance and mid-range strikes on Russian units and supply lines. insights.claim: Ukraine already uses Eutelsat's OneWeb as an alternative for some communications. But OneWeb has just over 600 satellites versus Starlink's 10,000, so it supports far less data and fewer customers. Its terminals are much bulkier and cost about 45 times more, which makes drone mounting harder.

insights.so_what: Eutelsat is the obvious near-term beneficiary, but it is limited by capacity and terminal cost, which caps how much Starlink share it can take.
